Humor in general is a really weird feature of human interaction. At its core, it has been theorized that a sense of humor is a coping mechanism we have developed through experience to deal with emotional pain. If this theory is true, it would imply that unfunny people have experienced little emotional pain in their lives, have an extreme tolerance for such pain, or have some other external coping mechanisms that have prohibited the development of a sense of humor.

So if this is the case, why would these people crack jokes at all? I believe it comes down to memes. No, not image macros, memes. Imitated behaviors. All successful social media sites have constructed systems that rewire our reward mechanisms. Social validation used to be delivered through body language and verbal communication, but now it has been distilled into a very binary, yes/no, up/down, black/white format that leaves no room for the nuance that would be seen in a random group of people in a room together.

The result of social media is an incredible density of human interaction, in which a user is able to survey behaviors that are approved of, and most will do their best to conform to those perceived expectations by imitating those who they perceive as being accepted by the group. This is not only the reason for commonalities in humor, but also for the idea of the "hivemind."

Its important to distinguish between people who make jokes, and those who laugh at them. The comedians among us (myself included) are always seeking validation of some sort. That much is natural. The people who laugh at (or in this case upvote) these bad jokes are the interesting ones.

TLDR: People choose their behaviors based on a combination of trial and error, and imitated behavior. Social media insures (through density of information) that the audience is always the same, which minimizes variation in behavior. Because the perceived "in-group" is dominated by sheltered and unfunny people, people who seek validation will themselves strive to be unfunny, even if they are not necessarily unfunny people.
